_comment: Baked by scripts/bake_updates.py from hebrish.app/changelog; do not edit by hand. Shown offline in the apps' What's new (Android Updates screen, desktop About tab).

entries.title: Daniel's story, a new support page, and breadcrumbs on model pages
entries.summary: About now opens with who makes Hebrish and why, with a real photo and some dictation facts.

entries.title: The training blend, and category charts
entries.summary: /models now explains the training blend: the five ingredients, what each one is for, and why LibriSpeech is in the mix, with Corn at the blender.

entries.title: Windows catches up
entries.summary: Windows and AppImage: a new stable build with everything since Windows 1.012.

entries.title: Paste last only pastes what was missed, and Corn on the start-up screen
entries.summary: Paste last: after an early Enter kept your last words out of a message, the Paste last key and tray item now paste only those words, not the whole take again.

entries.title: Licensing in the top menu, a clearer models page, and Corn
entries.summary: Licensing is now in the top menu and opens with what each part of Hebrish is licensed under, with the Creative Commons icons.

entries.title: See what each Sabich and Shakshuka version was trained on
entries.summary: /models now leads with the two models in active development, Sabich and Shakshuka, with a training explorer: hours of audio at each version, then clips, speakers, the blend and topics for any version you pick.

entries.title: Shakshuka v2.1
entries.summary: Shakshuka, the streaming model, is updated for the first time since Release v2. It continues from v2.0 and now knows the same recordings as Sabich: 1,672 minutes of them, up from 642.

entries.title: Switch models from the tray, one Sabich, and one Voice detection switch
entries.summary: Active model: switch between Sabich and Shakshuka from the tray menu, or with the new Select Sabich, Select Shakshuka and Toggle model action keys.

entries.title: Let your coding agent read your history, fix recurring errors and update the app
entries.summary: Agent control (opt-in): a new switch in Settings → Local API lets coding agents on this computer read and search your transcript history, add find-and-replace rules to the personal dictionary, update the app and its models, switch model and start or stop dictation.

entries.title: How the training sentences are made
entries.summary: A method note, How the Hebrish training sentences are made (PDF, 5 pages, with charts): where the words and sentences come from, how sentences are generated from a target term and its context, which models and batch APIs wrote them, the rejection policy, spelling and…

entries.title: How Hebrish will be licensed to organisations
entries.summary: A new Licensing page, also in Hebrew: free for individuals, research, education and small non-profits and volunteer organisations; an institutional licence for health funds, hospitals and public bodies; a commercial licence for businesses.

entries.title: Tell Daniel how Hebrish works for you
entries.summary: A short four-step form at the top of Feedback: where you use Hebrish, the model and version, your accent, an accuracy rating, the kinds of words it struggles with and a list of words it gets wrong.

entries.title: Transform a transcript into an email, a to-do list or minutes, and your clipboard comes back after a paste
entries.summary: Transform… (experimental): on the Transcription tab, rewrite a transcript with one of 206 ready-made prompts: a business or casual email, a to-do list, meeting minutes, a post, data formats and more.

entries.title: Send your own voice samples through Hugging Face
entries.summary: A batch of your own recordings can now be sent as a pull request on Hebrish/Community-Voice-Contributions, one folder per Hugging Face username.

entries.title: Sabich (Rolling) r1: the new default model in the apps
entries.summary: Sabich (Rolling) is Sabich v2.4 trained further from its own weights, for 6 more epochs, on all the recordings collected so far, instead of retraining from stock NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2.

entries.title: Download models in sets, update them all at once, and the title model downloads again
entries.summary: Bundles: the Models tab now starts with three sets you can download in one click. Everything (Sabich, Shakshuka, and the clean-up, title and paragraph models), Voice Typing (Sabich and Shakshuka) and Transcription (Sabich with the clean-up, title and paragraph models).

entries.title: Saved transcripts get a folder, a title and a proper header; transcripts arrive in one go
entries.summary: Save writes straight to a Hebrish folder (Documents, Hebrish, transcripts by default), one folder per year, month and day, as Markdown, and never overwrites.

entries.title: Press Enter after silence, a local transcription API, and no more lost pieces
entries.summary: Press Enter after silence (optional, off by default, Settings, Action keys): while Voice Typing with Insert as you go, once text has been typed and you have been quiet for 8 seconds (2 to 60), Hebrish presses your Send key once, so a message to Claude goes without reaching for…

entries.title: Sabich v2.3: 20% more recordings
entries.summary: Sabich v2.3 replaces v2.2 as the recommended model in the apps. It is a Sabich-only update to Release v2, trained the same way as v2.2 on 1,296 minutes of audio (522.8 minutes of English with Hebrew words in it, up from 471.4).

entries.title: Optional clean-up model, and a lighter, clearer app
entries.summary: Clean up (optional, off by default): download S1-ASR-Cleanup, a fine-tune of S1-mini by Superwhisper, under Models, Utilities, Post-processing (about 660 MB), and turn on Clean up there or in the Transcription tab.
